title: POC weekly eval sweep and scenario walkthrough with ZenWave
topics: prompt set regressions and threshold tuning
guardrail false positives and rollback scenarios
next steps: benchmark sweep and security docs
summary: Mid-poc sync focused on prompt-level regressions flagged over the last week, discussion of scoring thresholds, a guardrail false positive pattern for warranty-like language, and agreement to run a broad scenario sweep on a quantized dedicated variant plus provide SOC2/KMS docs. Owner assignments and a rollback drill scheduled.
questions: Can Redwood run a 1k prompt sweep on quantized small model and provide latency/cost distrib?
Will the guardrail be tuned per intent or global threshold?
What encryption/KMS options for the private deployment?
What's the expected fallback behavior on capacity spike for dedicated pool?
action_items: Marcus Patel: run 1,000-prompt sweep (diverse prompt set) on dedicated small-quantized model, deliver CSV with latency percentiles and token cost (due 2026-10-14)
Lara Chen: share SOC2 + KMS integration doc and private-deploy checklist with Tom and Priya (due 2026-10-09)
Priya Reddy: provide 150 additional edge-case prompts (warranty/legal style) for guardrail tuning (due 2026-10-11)
Tom Alvarez: schedule a 30-min rollback drill window for 2026-10-20 and confirm access to staging VPC (due 2026-10-12)
Marcus Patel: prototype per-intent guardrail thresholds and share a short RFC (due 2026-10-13)
next_steps: Run sweep and share bench CSV
Tune guardrail thresholds per intent, reduce false positives on warranty/verbatim clauses
Share security/compliance docs and private deployment checklist
Schedule rollback drill and final pilot acceptance criteria call
meeting_transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-07 14:30 PDT | Duration: ~42 minutes | Attendees: Lara Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Reddy (ZenWave Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (ZenWave SRE), Sara Nunez (ZenWave Product)

[00:00] Lara Chen: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time, quick check — audio ok?
[00:06] Priya Reddy: yea loud and clear, thanks Lara.
[00:10] Lara Chen: cool, agenda — quick results review, regression patterns priya flagged, then guardrail tuning options, and agree next steps. Marcus is gonna run through the numbers.
[00:20] Marcus Patel: yep, thanks. so high level we ran the latest eval set you gave us last week, about 850 prompt variants, split across intent buckets (support, returns, warranty, product-faq). overall accuracy by your scoring function is steady at ~87% but we spotted a cluster of regressions in the warranty/billing family.
[00:40] Tom Alvarez: yep that's what we saw in our heatmap — a spike in false positives where the model refused to answer or produced an irrelevant legal-safe reply, even when the prompt was neutral.
[00:53] Sara Nunez: to confirm, false positives meaning guardrail tripped? or meaning scoring flagged as low quality?
[00:58] Marcus Patel: guardrail tripped — the safer fallback kicked in. in a lot of these cases it seems the guardrail classifier is too sensitive to phrases like "under warranty" or "liability" even in benign contexts.
[01:12] Priya Reddy: yeah and that hurts our product flows — customers see a canned legal response which increases support tickets.
[01:20] Lara Chen: understoood. quick clarifying question: are those prompts more likely to be long, multi-sentence, or short?
[01:26] Marcus Patel: mixed — about 60% are short queries but with keywords that the intent classifier weights highly. could be a training imbalance.
[01:34] [01:34] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[01:40] Lara Chen: okay. so two levers here: we can (1) tune the classifier thresholds and introduce per-intent overrides, or (2) modify the fallback copy to be less canned while we fix thresholds. Marcus which is lower risk for rollout?
[01:55] Marcus Patel: threshold tuning is quick but needs careful calibration to avoid letting unsafe content slip. per-intent thresholds are best: e.g. returns/warranty get relaxed a bit, but security/legal stays tight. fallback copy is ops work — easy to change but doesn't fix the underlying misclassification.
[02:12] Priya Reddy: can we do both? conservative threshold relax per intent and softer fallback as a stopgap?
[02:18] Marcus Patel: yes. we recommend a staged approach: run a simulated sweep with proposed thresholds against your dataset and the 150 edge-case prompts Priya mentioned. measure false positive reduction vs false negative increase.
[02:32] Tom Alvarez: on sim sweeps — what model variant are you using for the sweep currently? hosted latest small or the dedicated quantized one?
[02:40] Marcus Patel: this last sweep was on the hosted baseline (gpt-ish open model we onboarded). since you asked about latency and cost we can replicate on the dedicated quantized path — that will give you realistic P95/P99 for your planned dedicated pool.
[02:53] Priya Reddy: please run it on the quantized dedicated variant. we saw production latency slightly better than hosted but want the distribution.
[02:59] Lara Chen: just to call out tradeoffs — quantized dedicated will reduce cost per token but may slightly increase tail latency under heavy KV cache misses; we'll surface percentiles.
[03:12] Sara Nunez: what's the expected difference in token cost? rough ballpark.
[03:16] Marcus Patel: ballpark — 30-40% cheaper per token for int8 small quantized on the dedicated pool vs hosted standard. exact depends on sequence length and batching. we'll include cost-per-1k tokens estimate.
[03:29] [03:29] Speaker 2: background noise
[03:36] Lara Chen: ok good. next item: fallback behavior and rollback drill. Tom, you said security wanted a drill to ensure controlled rollback in case of a quality regression?
[03:45] Tom Alvarez: yeah we need to validate the canary and rollback playbook. in our staging we'd like to simulate a spike in regression rate and observe automated fallback to a more conservative model and then to cached answers. questions on redwood side — how fast can dedicated routing change under load?
[03:59] Marcus Patel: our routing policy supports immediate fallback to a pinned conservative variant within seconds; but if you're on a reserved capacity pool the autoscaling delay is different — we'll document exact numbers. for the rollback drill we recommend: (a) trigger via the console, (b) observe traffic shift, (c) validate log/audit entries, (d) restore.
[04:18] Priya Reddy: audit logs — we need to ensure token-level tracing but also masked PII. does Redwood provide redaction hooks?
[04:26] Marcus Patel: yes we support pre-ingest redaction and token masking, plus KMS integration for encrypted logs. for private deployments we can tie into your HSM. Lara will share the KMS integration doc.
[04:37] Lara Chen: i'll share the doc after this call. Tom — anything specific you need from our support team to run the drill?
[04:44] Tom Alvarez: access to staging VPC and a test API key with the same routing/pools as prod. and a contact for the 30-min window in case we need to flip.
[04:52] Lara Chen: we'll coordinate that.
[04:54] Sara Nunez: quick question on scoring: our current evaluation function weights safety heavily which may penalize helpfulness. can we tweak scoring to put more weight on relevance for the product-faq intent?
[05:06] Marcus Patel: yes scoring is configurable per-intent. we'll propose new weights and run the sweep to show changes to final score and PR curve.
[05:15] Priya Reddy: also we noticed a few hallucinations in product details for SKU-like prompts — lower severity but noticeable. any idea why?
[05:23] Marcus Patel: hallucinations often correlate with training data coverage; for SKU-specific answers we recommend retrieval augmentation or a stronger grounding signal. two options: integrate your SKU DB as a retrieval step, or tighten the generation response length and prefer structured outputs with cited facts.
[05:40] Priya Reddy: retrieval sounds good — what's the added latency?
[05:42] Marcus Patel: depends on your vector DB and cache hit rate. with prefix/KV caching and local caching on dedicated pool, median added ~40-120 ms on top of generation; can be negligible if strong caching hits. we'll include latency breakdown in the sweep.
[05:58] [06:00] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[06:05] Lara Chen: moving on to guardrail tuning specifics — Marcus, can you explain per-intent thresholds and how we'd operationalize them?
[06:12] Marcus Patel: sure. right now the guardrail classifier returns a score 0-1 and a generic decision threshold is applied globally. per-intent thresholds allow e.g. for product-faq: threshold=0.6, warranty: 0.55, legal: 0.85. we expose this in the console and in the API as a routing policy. changes can be rolled out with canaries.
[06:31] Tom Alvarez: will changes to thresholds be auditable? we need history and who changed what.
[06:36] Lara Chen: yes our console keeps audit logs of threshold changes and you can push via API with role-based permissions.
[06:43] Priya Reddy: what's the rollback granularity — can we rollback only the warranty threshold without affecting others?
[06:48] Marcus Patel: yes thresholds are atomic per intent; you can rollback single-intent settings.
[06:53] Sara Nunez: great. small UX ask — instead of a binary canned fallback, could the model offer a partial answer with a "needs follow-up" flag?
[07:01] Marcus Patel: absolutely. that's the graded-fallback pattern — we can return a structured object: {answer, confidence, follow_up_required}. note: this will be in the structured output route.
[07:15] Priya Reddy: ok that would help reduce support friction.
[07:18] Lara Chen: on the topic of structured outputs — are you using tool-calling or function/call style responses in your current flows?
[07:24] Priya Reddy: currently no, just pure text generation. product is open to moving to structured for SKU and warranty flows.
[07:30] Marcus Patel: we can demo tiny tool-call prototype next week. it helps grounding.
[07:34] [07:34] Speaker 2: (typing)
[07:40] Lara Chen: let's talk timeline. Marcus — how long to run the 1k sweep on dedicated quantized and produce the CSV with P50/P95/P99, token cost, and failure modes?
[07:49] Marcus Patel: estimate 4 business days to run and validate — so deliverable by 2026-10-14. includes per-intent guardrail sim.
[07:57] Priya Reddy: perfect. one more ask: we need the SOC2 + KMS doc for procurement — can you attach certs?
[08:05] Lara Chen: yes, I'll attach our SOC2 type II report and the KMS/HSM integration guide. note: for private deployments we can do customer-supplied HSM keys.
[08:16] Tom Alvarez: regarding encryption at rest for logs — can we obfuscate PII for audit while still keeping token counts for cost tracking?
[08:24] Marcus Patel: yes, logs can be redacted pre-ingest; token billing is independent and we can still report token usage metrics without raw text.
[08:32] Priya Reddy: ok that addresses procurement concerns.
[08:35] Lara Chen: quick check — any new blockers or blockers lifted since last week?
[08:40] Sara Nunez: blocker: we still need 150 specific warranty edge-case prompts; lifting: we resolved the vector DB connectivity issue in staging so retrieval test is possible.
[08:50] Lara Chen: thanks. Marcus, can you summarize the proposed guardrail change set you'll try in the sweep?
[08:57] Marcus Patel: yes — (1) relax warranty/product-faq thresholds by 0.05, (2) leave legal/security thresholds unchanged, (3) enable soft fallback copy with graded-fallback flag for product-faq, (4) run per-intent PR curve analysis and produce recommended settings and rollback points.
[09:15] Priya Reddy: sounds good. also we want the sweep to include a run with retrieval-on and retrieval-off to compare hallucination counts.
[09:23] Marcus Patel: noted — will include both modes.
[09:26] Lara Chen: Tom, any infra requests for the dedicated-run?
[09:29] Tom Alvarez: we need the test API key and staging VPC routes; also want to confirm burst capacity behavior — what happens when reserved pool saturates?
[09:38] Marcus Patel: if pool saturates we have routing fallback options: burst to hosted if enabled, or queue requests based on latency SLOs; we can enforce strict capacity via rejection or route to a slower but cheaper fallback. we'll document recommended policies.
[09:53] [10:00] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[10:05] Lara Chen: ok wrapping up with explicit next steps and owners — I'm going to outline them and we can all agree.
[10:13] Lara Chen: Marcus will run the 1k sweep on dedicated quantized and deliver by Oct 14. Marcus will also prototype per-intent threshold RFC and share by Oct 13.
[10:25] Marcus Patel: correct.
[10:27] Lara Chen: Priya will share the 150 edge-case prompts by Oct 11.
[10:32] Priya Reddy: will do.
[10:34] Lara Chen: Tom to confirm staging access and schedule rollback drill window by Oct 12.
[10:39] Tom Alvarez: yes can do.
[10:42] Lara Chen: I'll send SOC2 and KMS docs within 48 hours.
[10:46] Lara Chen: any other items before we close?
[10:50] Sara Nunez: one tiny follow-up: can we get a short note on how prefix/KV caching behaves with dedicated quantized models? just the top bullet points.
[10:58] Marcus Patel: sure will include that in the sweep report. caching bullets: hot KV cache retains recent prefixes in GPU memory, cache hit reduces latency by ~30-60ms, cold-starts pay miss penalty.
[11:12] Lara Chen: perfect. ok thanks everyone. we'll send notes and recs.
[11:17] Priya Reddy: thanks all.
[11:20] Tom Alvarez: thanks.
[11:22] Marcus Patel: thanks, bye.
[11:24] Lara Chen: bye.

Transcript notes: occasional brief gaps and minor transcription errors present. timestamps are approximate and put every ~20-90 seconds for reference.
